Agent1.reasoning: The superconducting magnet generating the main magnetic field is absolutely fundamental to MRI operation - no MRI can function without it. This is universally standard across all MRI systems.
RF transmitter and receiver coils are essential for excitation and signal detection in MRI. Every MRI system requires this component for magnetic resonance signal generation and reception.
Gradient coils (X, Y, Z) are critical for spatial encoding and slice selection. They create the controlled magnetic field variations necessary for image formation in all MRI systems.
A motorized patient table/bed is required for precise patient positioning within the magnetic field. This is a distinct manufactured component present in all MRI systems.
Dedicated high-performance computing hardware for image reconstruction and processing is essential. While varying in specification, this is a distinct primary component.
Helium cooling system maintaining superconducting magnet at 4K is critical for magnet operation. This is a complex, distinct manufacturing component in superconducting MRI systems.
RF and magnetic shielding protect against interference and contain magnetic fields. This includes room shielding and integrated system shielding as primary safety components.
Operator interface and system control hardware is a distinct manufactured component, though implementations vary significantly between manufacturers.
High-power electrical systems for magnet, gradients, and RF are essential components, though often distributed across multiple subsystems.
